sections.title: Decide who comes. Reward the ones who keep coming.
sections.lead: Open booking or applications, a balanced room, and memberships that give your regulars a better price. Every rupee by UPI or card, next to the right name.

sections.title: Decide who gets a place, event by event.

items.title: Open
items.body: Anyone can book. A page with places left. Book and pay in a couple of taps.

items.title: Applications
items.body: They apply, you choose. Ask what you want to know with your own form. Approve with a tap.

items.title: Invite-only
items.body: A private link. Only people with your invite link or code can book.

items.title: Private offer
items.body: A place for one person. Send someone their own checkout link, checked against their phone number.

sections.statusNote: Approval scope on applications (this event, a series, all future events), approved guests skipping the form and members approved automatically are not built. Show this when they ship.
sections.title: Approve someone once, not every time.
sections.lead: Someone new to your community fills in your application form. You approve them for this event, or for everything you run, so next time they just book. Your regulars never wait in a queue again.
ticks: Approve for one event, for a series, or for every event you host
Approved guests skip the form and book straight away
Approval lives on their guest record, so you can change it any time
Members can be approved automatically

sections.title: Keep the room balanced, by itself.
sections.lead: Set how many places go to women and how many to men, or no limits at all, and an age range for the night. When a group fills, the rest of the room stays open.
ticks: A cap for women and a cap for men, or none
An age range for each event
Set once on the event, and every booking is checked against it

sections.statusNote: Caps are built for women and men. The third capped group (non-binary or other), asking guests without a gender once at booking, and a waitlist per group are decided (18 Nov) but not built. Show this in place of the band above when they ship.
sections.title: Keep the room balanced, by itself.
sections.lead: Set how many places go to women, to men, and to non-binary and other guests, and an age range for the night. When one group fills, new bookings from it join the waitlist, and the rest of the room stays open.
ticks: A cap for each group: women, men, and non-binary or other. Or no limits at all
An age range, checked against the date of birth on the guest’s profile
A waitlist for each group, so a cancellation goes to the right person
Guests only see whether they can book, never your numbers. Anyone who hasn’t shared their gender is asked once, at booking

sections.title: Turn regulars into members.
sections.lead: Sell a monthly or yearly membership with your own perks. Members pay less for tickets, book before everyone else and get into members-only nights. You get income that doesn’t depend on the next event selling out.
ticks: Monthly and annual plans, with a free trial if you want one
Member prices for each event: a discount, or free
Early access: members can book before general sale opens
Members-only events, and a cap on how many members you take
Paid through Razorpay, and renewed each month or year

sections.title: Full events fill themselves. Payments match themselves.

items.title: Waitlists that move
items.body: When someone drops out of a free event, the next person moves up. On a paid one, send an offer that stays open for as long as you choose, up to a day.

items.title: Questions with the booking
items.body: Dietary needs, a T-shirt size or a signed waiver, asked with a form. Answers go on the guest’s record.

items.title: Booking for friends
items.body: Up to four places in one booking, with a name for each guest.

items.title: UPI or card
items.body: Paid at booking through Razorpay. Every payment lands next to the right name.

items.title: Refunds by your rules
items.body: Set a cancellation policy for each event, and refunds follow it.

items.title: Paid to you
items.body: By default, guests pay into your own Razorpay account. {{brand.name}} bills its fee afterwards.

sections.foot: 5% of ticket and membership sales, never more than ₹10,000 a month · Free events stay free · 30 days free from your first event

sections.kicker: Try it with your next event
sections.title: Start your next event on {{brand.name}} from a link you already have.

ticks: The event’s name, date and start time, read from your link
A page with several events? Choose the one to bring over
A private draft in your city: no one can see or book it
Waiting in {{brand.stores.hostAppName}} when you sign in with the same phone number

leadForm.label: Link to an event
leadForm.note: Private until you claim it. Takes about a minute.

items.question: Can I approve each guest myself?
items.answer: Yes. Turn on applications, ask your questions, and approve or decline each person. Approved guests pay to confirm their place.

items.question: Can I balance the room by gender?
items.answer: Yes. Set how many places go to women and how many to men, or leave it open.

items.question: Can I set an age range?
How do memberships work?
items.answer: You create plans with a monthly or annual price and choose the perks: member prices, early access and members-only events. Members pay through Razorpay, and the membership renews by itself.

items.question: Can members come for free?
items.answer: Yes. Set the member price for an event to free, and members book without paying.

items.question: What happens when someone cancels?
items.answer: Refunds follow the cancellation policy you set for the event. On a free event, the next person on the waitlist gets the place; on a paid one, you can send waitlisted guests an offer.

items.question: Where does the money go?
items.answer: By default, into your own Razorpay account, and from there to your bank on Razorpay’s usual schedule. Setting up Razorpay includes its KYC check, which usually takes 1 to 2 working days. Free events don’t need it.

items.question: Do regulars have to apply every time?
items.answer: No. Approve someone for all your events and they book straight away from then on. You can change that on their record whenever you like.
